coordinateSystem: All x, y, width and height values are percentages of the full image, with origin at top-left.
formatPreference: Full-resolution WebP files are the runtime and zoom assets. Original PNG authoring masters are archived outside the application repository.
reviewScope: Illustrative visual recognition only. Visible geometry has been reviewed; these are not manufacturer drawings, dimensions, maintenance instructions, or authoritative lesson terminology.
labelPolicy: Semantic region names describe the depicted object only. Map labels and approved lesson terminology to the course source before use. No text or arrows are baked into these assets.

assets.subject: Assembled high-wing, single-engine light airplane with selected near-wing and fuselage skin removed.
depictedGeometry: Recognizable full aircraft silhouette
Spanwise member and chordwise ribs in the near wing
Transverse fuselage frames and lengthwise members
High-wing support strut
Conventional tail and visible landing gear
limitations: Generic illustrative aircraft, not a model-specific maintenance drawing.
Some far-side gear is occluded; do not use the view to count visible wheels.
Member sizes, spacing, joints and load paths are illustrative and not dimensionally verified.

assets.subject: Three separate construction specimens: tubular triangulated frame, mostly unstiffened shell, shell with frames and lengthwise stiffeners.
depictedGeometry: Left: triangulated tubular frame with a small fabric-like covering section
Center: mostly empty cylindrical shell with end/forming rings
Right: cylindrical skin supported by circular frames and continuous lengthwise stiffeners
limitations: The left specimen depicts a tubular/truss structure; it must not automatically be labeled 'fuselaje compuesto'. Resolve that course terminology from the approved source.
Center and right may support a source-grounded monocoque / semimonocoque comparison, but joints, wall thicknesses and exact frame spacing are illustrative.
No material-strength or load-distribution claim is established by the image alone.

assets.subject: Four external, closed-case engines with distinct cylinder arrangements: inline four, V banks, horizontal opposed four, and single-row five-cylinder radial.
depictedGeometry: Top-left: four upright finned cylinders in one row with closed crankcase
Top-right: two inclined finned cylinder banks with a shared closed central case
Bottom-left: two horizontal finned cylinders on each side of a closed central case
Bottom-right: five outward-pointing cylinders in a near-regular five-spoke pattern around a closed round central case
limitations: Use for recognizing layout only, not crankshaft/connecting-rod kinematics, valve timing, firing order, engine dimensions, or engine-model identification.
Every barrel and crankcase is closed; internal pistons, rods and crankshafts are intentionally not depicted. Use the separate cylinder closeup for parts teaching.
The five-cylinder radial uses an improved near-regular five-spoke pattern. The generated rendering is illustrative rather than dimensioned; do not infer exact angular spacing from pixels.
assets.reviewStatus: Refined exterior-only variant, visually checked after closing all cutaway windows. Four distinct arrangements and five radial cylinders remain visible.

assets.subject: Single static air-cooled piston-cylinder cutaway with two overhead poppet valves, central spark plug, piston, rod and lower case.
limitations: Static parts-recognition image only; do not animate over the fixed piston or valves as if this showed changing stroke states.
Simplified generic cylinder, not a specific aircraft engine or complete ignition installation.

assets.subject: Four matched head/cylinder/piston views with corrected visibly distinct open-versus-seated poppet valve states.
assets.requiredPresentation: Use the head-cylinder crop regions below, not the full plate. Add any motion arrows in code outside the raster and obtain phase wording from the approved source.
depictedGeometry: Top-left: left valve lowered from its seat, right valve seated, piston below head
Top-right: both valves seated, piston near head
Bottom-left: both valves seated, piston below head, warm chamber fill
Bottom-right: right valve lowered from its seat, left valve seated, piston below head
limitations: The lower generated connecting-rod lengths and crank offsets are not consistent enough for kinematics teaching. They are excluded from the approved crop regions.
Still images cannot themselves establish upward/downward motion; use source-grounded code overlays or captions.
Open-valve lift is visually exaggerated so seated versus open states remain clear at lesson size.
Gas colors are explanatory visual conventions, not actual gas colors.
The generic static closeup and these state images must not be interchanged as equivalent phase geometry.

assets.subject: Head/cylinder/piston still showing simultaneous open intake and exhaust valves with the piston near the top of its travel.
assets.requiredPresentation: Use as a detail of valve overlap during the exhaust-to-intake transition. Do not present it as a fifth stroke or as ignition/compression.
depictedGeometry: Left single-piece poppet valve lowered from its fixed seat, leaving an open inlet passage
Right single-piece poppet valve lowered simultaneously, leaving an open outlet passage
Piston near the top of the illustrated cylinder with visible clearance below both valve heads
Inactive central spark plug; no combustion flame or lower linkage
assets.reviewStatus: Visually reviewed after removing apparent duplicated discs and increasing both open-seat gaps. Each valve is a single connected stem/head; both passages visibly open with clearance above piston.
limitations: Qualitative illustration only; valve lift and clearance are emphasized for visibility and are not dimensioned or mechanically certified.
Do not infer exact crank angle, overlap duration, timing values or piston-to-valve clearance from this still.
Blue/red ports are explanatory visual conventions. Both valves being open represents overlap between exhaust and intake, not an additional stroke.
No lower connecting-rod/crankshaft geometry is included.

assets.subject: Single conventional pushrod-operated overhead valve train with an exposed contact chain and fixed central rocker pivot.
assets.requiredPresentation: Identify this as one conventional pushrod architecture. Use source-grounded labels; do not imply all engines use this arrangement.
depictedGeometry: Bottom-left eccentric cam lobe in contact with underside of a tappet in its guide
Single straight pushrod beside the cylinder, with ball ends seated in tappet and rocker cups
Rocker supported by an obvious central pivot shaft on a bolted fixed pedestal
Rocker opposite end contacts valve-stem tip above a spring and guide
Single open mushroom valve head below a closely matching fixed seat; no piston or crankshaft mechanism
assets.reviewStatus: All five interfaces visually checked: cam-to-tappet, tappet-to-pushrod, pushrod-to-rocker, fixed rocker pivot, rocker-to-valve tip. No crossed or disconnected rods observed.
limitations: Conventional explanatory example only, not universal engine architecture or a model-specific maintenance drawing.
Static raised-cam/open-valve state; geometry does not specify exact lift, rocker ratio, clearances, cam profile, dimensions or timing.
No piston, connecting rod, crankshaft, complete lubrication circuit or full valve-cover assembly is shown.
Material colors and cutaway castings clarify the chain; they are not a material specification.
